newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel revises up German '96 federal overshoot.
newsitem.headline: Waigel revises up German '96 federal overshoot.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel on Wednesday revised up the final federal budget deficit for 1996 to 78.3 billion marks, representing an overshoot of 18.4 billion marks from the budgeted target.

Federal spending in 1996 totalled 455.6 billion marks, up from an originally planned 451.3 billion marks, Waigel said in a statement. The federal deficit covers spending by the Bonn government, but does not include state and municipal outgoings.
Waigel said that Germany's total public sector deficit was equivalent to 3.9 percent of gross domestic product in 1996.

The statement added the budget result made Germany's fiscal situation more difficult, and to meet borrowing limits set in the Maastricht treaty on monetary union "it will be necessary to continue our savings course with greater determination."

Waigel said the "unfavourable result" stemmed from weak economic growth of 1.4 percent last year, which fell short of forecasts in October 1995 by the government and an advisory panel of six leading institutes of 2.5 percent growth on which the 1996 budget was based.

Higher unemployment resulted in 17 billion marks in extra state spending to finance jobless benefits, while tax revenues fell short by 17 billion marks. Extra costs could only be partly offset by spending cuts, Waigel said.
